Specimen ontology rules, version 2.0. Each rule names its Darwin Core term and how it is checked.
- one_collecting_event: A specimen has one collecting event. When two of its labels write two different collecting dates, or two place names (letter case, accents, punctuation and unit words such as "Dept." aside) that no source the answer cites confirms as one place, an answer that settles the field on one label's text is refused. (Darwin Core: Event: eventDate; dcterms:Location: locality; checked by code.)
- place_within_settled_places: When a place value is applied, the check of its larger places refuses a place below the country whose source names no larger place, one whose source puts it outside the country settled for its reading, a county or a city outside the province settled for its reading, and a county that is that province itself. (Darwin Core: country, stateProvince, county, municipality; checked by code.)
- place_chain: The places form one chain, country > province or state > county > city. A settled value outside the chain settled above it is marked for a person, including what the refusal at apply time lets pass (a settled Coles County, then an exact "Chicago" under Illinois), and so is a chain that derivation fills when it breaks the chain. (Darwin Core: country, stateProvince, county, municipality; not yet checked.)
- date_order: The collecting date is on or before the determination date; the same day is allowed. Dates written at different precisions compare on the parts both have ("1946" and "1946-09-06" agree). A determination dated before the collecting date is marked for a person, both dates listed. (Darwin Core: eventDate, dateIdentified; not yet checked.)
- day_month_order: The date check reads a numeric date whose two orders, day-month and month-day, give two different dates both ways and settles neither reading, a conflict with both readings for a person; a numeric date whose two orders give one date (5-5-48) settles on it. (Darwin Core: eventDate, dateIdentified; checked by code.)
- code_is_no_date: A slide or preparation code is never a date, nor is any part of it: text that stands inside a longer hyphen-joined code in any reading is no date. (Darwin Core: ours: no Darwin Core term fits a code; eventDate; checked by code.)
- label_type_routing: A label's type (locality, determination, code) sends its units to the experts of its fields first and never keeps a field's expert from a unit: a determination label that writes a locality reaches the locality expert. (Darwin Core: ours: no Darwin Core term fits a label; not yet checked.)
- elevation_unit_feet: An elevation whose cleared text writes no unit is read as feet only when (a) at least one reader wrote the foot mark or "ft" at this unit, (b) the number read as metres is above the highest point of the specimen's country, which is cleared, not marked (the highest-point table), and (c) the number read as feet is possible (16000 with a mark is not, in the Philippines). When all hold, the elevation settles in feet, cleared, its reason "Basis: inferred, rule elevation_unit_feet". Without (a) the field is unresolved: magnitude alone never decides; so it is when (b) or (c) fails or the country is marked. Terrain takes no part while the owner's decision D5 is held. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; not yet checked.)
- elevation_needs_a_unit: An answer that settles an elevation field on a number that one of its readings writes with no unit is refused: a unit is never guessed from the magnitude, the place or a map. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- elevation_unit_decides_field: An answer that settles an elevation field on a number that one of its readings writes in the other unit is refused. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- place_parents_derived: Upward derivation: a derived country, province or state, or county is the parent that the source of a settled place below it names at that level; it never replaces a value settled from the label; no parent is derived where settled places below name different ones there; and a county is never derived from a city whose source names fewer than three larger places, nor a province from a county whose source names fewer than two. (Darwin Core: country, stateProvince, county; checked by code.)
- elevation_conversion: A derived elevation is a stated one copied to the other end of its unit, or its exact conversion (1 ft = 0.3048 m) rounded to the hundredth; a derived elevation never replaces a stated one; and no elevation is derived while an elevation field is neither settled nor open (one the readings disagree on goes to a person first). (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- end_date_from_one_date: A derived Date Visited To is the date of a settled Date Visited From, at its precision, and is never derived from a written range. (Darwin Core: eventDate; checked by code.)
- precise_location_extent: Precise Location is the label's locality as written: every line of its locality text, with its line breaks, the higher places and an elevation written among those lines included. It is never cut to the first line, and a label whose locality names nothing finer than its town still has a Precise Location: those lines as written. (Darwin Core: verbatimLocality; not yet checked.)

Not rules:
- taxon_regional_occurrence: A taxon's regional occurrence is not a rule: that an authority records no occurrence of a taxon in a region does not make it impossible there, and no check uses occurrence while the owner's decision D4 is held. (Darwin Core: scientificName; dcterms:Location.)
